components.name: get_current_user
components.description: The authenticated customer's id, from the X-Customer header

decisions.question: What does it provide, and for how long (one request, the whole app)?
decisions.answer: The customer id (str) from the X-Customer header, for one request

decisions.question: What happens when it cannot (no token, the database is down): which error, which HTTP status in the end?
decisions.answer: Header missing or empty: 401 Unauthorized

components.name: logging_setup
components.description: Configures logging once, at the app's startup - the only place that configures it (ARCH059 - no basicConfig, handler or root level anywhere else); every module takes its own logger with logging.getLogger(__name__). Level from the settings, one line per event with the request id, never a secret, a token or personal data; the tests put the logging back as it was after each test (a shared fixture of tests/conftest.py - later logs must not write to a test's closed stream).

decisions.question: Where do the logs go and in which format - e.g. stderr, one line per event with time, level, request id and message?
decisions.answer: stderr, one line per event: time, level, request id, message

components.name: settings
components.description: The service's settings, read from the environment (pydantic-settings), never from code.

decisions.question: Which settings, with which defaults (name: type = default), and which are required?
decisions.answer: app_name: str = 'orders'; nothing else yet

decisions.question: Which settings are secrets (never logged, never in a response), and where do they come from?
decisions.answer: No secret yet

components.name: new_order
components.description: What a customer sends to create an order: amount Decimal > 0

decisions.question: Which fields are required, and which are optional (with which default)?
decisions.answer: amount required

decisions.question: Which values are valid for each field (ranges, formats, lengths, allowed states)?
decisions.answer: amount > 0 with at most 2 decimals

decisions.question: Which fields must never appear in a response or a log (passwords, internal ids, personal data)?
decisions.answer: None

components.name: order
components.description: An order: id int, customer str, amount Decimal >= 0, status pending | paid | cancelled

decisions.question: Which fields are required, and which are optional (with which default)?
decisions.answer: All fields required

decisions.question: Which values are valid for each field (ranges, formats, lengths, allowed states)?
decisions.answer: amount >= 0 with 2 decimals; status pending, paid or cancelled

decisions.question: Which fields must never appear in a response or a log (passwords, internal ids, personal data)?
decisions.answer: None: the customer id is returned only to its owner

components.name: order_not_found
components.description: The order does not exist, or belongs to another customer

decisions.question: Which HTTP status does the app answer with it (404, 409, 422...)?
decisions.answer: 404 Not Found

decisions.question: What does its message say - and never say (internal ids, personal data, whether the resource exists)?
decisions.answer: "Order not found" - never the id's owner, never whether it exists

components.name: orders
components.description: Stores and finds orders (in memory to start)

decisions.question: Not found: return None, or raise which domain error?
decisions.answer: Return None

decisions.question: Who opens and commits the transaction (the service, never the repository)?
decisions.answer: No transaction: memory; the service decides what is saved

decisions.question: Two updates of the same record at the same time: last write wins, a version check, or a lock?
decisions.answer: Last write wins: an order is only created, never updated yet

decisions.question: Which queries can return many rows, and what is their maximum?
decisions.answer: None: no list query yet

P.retention.answer: In memory: gone when the service stops; nothing kept, nothing to erase on request

P.location.answer: The service's own memory, in the EU

components.name: create_order
components.description: Create a pending order for the current customer and save it

decisions.question: What does it do, step by step (read, check, change, save, call)?
decisions.answer: Build a pending order with the next id, save it, return it

decisions.question: Something it needs does not exist: which domain error?
decisions.answer: Not applicable: it needs nothing that may be missing

decisions.question: Called twice with the same input (a client retry): same result and no duplicate effect (idempotent), or a duplicate error?
decisions.answer: Two orders: a retry is a new order (customers cancel the extra one)

decisions.question: Who may perform it, and is that checked here or in the router?
decisions.answer: Any authenticated customer, for themselves; checked by the router

decisions.question: What must be all or nothing (one transaction), and what happens if a call to another service fails in the middle?
decisions.answer: One save, nothing else to undo

components.name: get_order
components.description: Return one order of the current customer

decisions.question: What does it do, step by step (read, check, change, save, call)?
decisions.answer: Find the order; check it belongs to the customer; return it

decisions.question: Something it needs does not exist: which domain error?
decisions.answer: OrderNotFoundError - also when it belongs to someone else, so ids reveal nothing

decisions.question: Called twice with the same input (a client retry): same result and no duplicate effect (idempotent), or a duplicate error?
decisions.answer: Same result: it only reads

decisions.question: Who may perform it, and is that checked here or in the router?
decisions.answer: The owner only; checked here

decisions.question: What must be all or nothing (one transaction), and what happens if a call to another service fails in the middle?
decisions.answer: Nothing to undo: it only reads

components.name: main
components.description: The service: the order routes under /v1, domain errors mapped to HTTP statuses

decisions.question: Which routers, under which prefix (e.g. /v1)?
decisions.answer: orders_router under /v1

decisions.question: Which domain errors map to which HTTP status (not found -> 404, conflict -> 409...)?
decisions.answer: OrderNotFoundError -> 404, as decided by the error

decisions.question: What happens at startup and shutdown (lifespan: connections, warm-up), and what if startup fails?
decisions.answer: Nothing to start or stop yet

decisions.question: CORS: which origins may call it from a browser - or none?
decisions.answer: No CORS: not called from browsers

decisions.question: Who may call each route: anyone, an authenticated user, the owner of the resource, which role?
decisions.answer: Authenticated customers (get_current_user), each only on their own orders

decisions.question: Status codes: success, not found, conflict, forbidden - and the error body format?
decisions.answer: 201 created, 200 read, 404 not found; errors as {"detail": "..."}

decisions.question: Invalid input: FastAPI's 422, or 400 with your own error format?
decisions.answer: FastAPI's 422

decisions.question: Lists: pagination, default and maximum page size - or no list route?
decisions.answer: No list route; POST repeated: two orders (no idempotency key yet)

decisions.question: A POST or PUT repeated by a client retry: an idempotency key, or duplicates accepted?
decisions.answer: No list route; POST repeated: two orders (no idempotency key yet)

P.purpose.answer: Take and show the orders of each customer, for that customer only

P.legal_basis.answer: Contract: the customer's orders (terms of sale)
